name: PRESIDENTIAL MATH
clue: Losing to Benjamin Harrison, then beating him 4 years later, made him both the 22nd and the 24th president

name: PLAY IT AGAIN
clue: Based on the unproduced play 'Everybody Comes to Rick's,' this 1943 Best Picture winner never has anyone say 'Play it again, Sam'

name: CARBON COPIES
clue: Named from the Greek for 'to write,' this soft, slippery mineral in your pencil is chemically identical to a diamond

name: CRUMBS OF WISDOM
clue: A fixture of American Chinese restaurants, it was likely invented by Japanese immigrants in California and is rare in China

name: SHUTTER TO THINK
clue: Her 1936 'Migrant Mother,' shot in a California pea pickers' camp, became the face of the Great Depression

name: FRAME JOB
clue: Picasso was questioned over its 1911 theft, but an ex-Louvre worker had it in a trunk, resurfacing in Florence 2 years later

name: MAJOR TRADITIONS
clue: Golf's other 3 majors rotate venues, but this one has never left the Georgia course where it debuted in 1934

name: FIT FOR A QUEEN
clue: Legend says a Naples pizzaiolo honored an 1889 royal visit with this pie, its tomato, mozzarella & basil matching Italy's flag

name: COVER STORIES
clue: Eric Blair, a onetime colonial policeman in Burma, took his pen name from a Suffolk river and gave the world Big Brother

name: BELOW SEA LEVEL
clue: Earth's lowest dry land rings this lake between Israel & Jordan, so salty that bathers float like corks

name: OPENING SENTENCES
clue: 'Happy families are all alike; every unhappy family is unhappy in its own way' opens this Tolstoy novel

name: AFRICAN COASTLINES
clue: Separated from Europe by the Strait of Gibraltar, it's the only African nation with both Mediterranean & Atlantic coasts

name: AGE OF EXPLORATION
clue: Magellan never finished the voyage; this Basque navigator brought the Victoria home in 1522 to complete the first circumnavigation

name: OLYMPIC CITIES
clue: Host of the 1948 'Austerity Games,' in 2012 it became the first city to stage the Summer Olympics three times

name: DRAWING THE LINE
clue: The meridian this 1494 pact drew through the Atlantic is the reason Brazil speaks Portuguese while its neighbors speak Spanish

name: MR. NICE GUY
clue: In 1969 this Presbyterian minister saved $20 million for public TV by reciting a gentle lyric to a gruff Senate chairman

name: FIRST EMPERORS
clue: Thousands of clay soldiers guard the tomb of this unifier of China in 221 B.C., who died chasing immortality with mercury elixirs

name: STRANGER THAN FICTION
clue: British naturalists in 1799 searched its first specimen for stitches, sure this egg-laying, duck-billed mammal was a hoax

name: TREE'S COMPANY
clue: The Americas' only Portuguese-speaking nation is named for a tree whose ember-red heartwood dyed European textiles

name: SAVED BY THE SIGNAL
clue: Its 1889 World's Fair permit ran only 20 years; what saved it from the scrap heap was its usefulness as a radio antenna

name: DATELINE: PACIFIC
clue: In 1995 this island republic bent the International Date Line eastward, uniting its atolls in one day and one millennium

name: DISTANT TOUCHDOWNS
clue: The 2005 Huygens landing, the most distant ever, touched down on this hazy Saturn moon where rivers run with liquid methane

name: TRIPLE CROWN
clue: Nicknamed the 'Test of the Champion,' this mile-and-a-half race is the longest leg of horse racing's Triple Crown

name: DUTCH MASTERS
clue: Centuries of grimy varnish gave his 1642 militia scene, actually set in daylight, the misleading nickname 'The Night Watch'

name: A DARK & STORMY NIGHT
clue: A rainy 1816 summer at Lord Byron's Lake Geneva villa spawned this novel subtitled 'The Modern Prometheus'

name: WHAT'S IN A PLACE NAME
clue: Stilt houses on Lake Maracaibo reminded explorers of Venice, so they gave this country a name meaning 'Little Venice'

name: UNIFORM DECISION
clue: In 1997, 50 years after his Brooklyn debut, this pioneer's No. 42 was retired by every team in Major League Baseball

name: NOBEL LITERATURE
clue: He wrote the national anthems of both India and Bangladesh, and in 1913 became the first non-European Nobel laureate

name: AN EMBARRASSMENT OF RICHES
clue: This Mali emperor's gold-strewing 1324 pilgrimage to Mecca was so lavish it reportedly tanked gold prices in Cairo for a decade

name: UNITS OF MEASURE
clue: The SI unit of magnetic flux density is named for this inventor, born in 1856 in a village in what is now Croatia
